author: Maya Yang
description:
Ruling said law enacted by Congress reflects preference for border control over environmental and recreational harm

The US supreme court has allowed Donald Trump to continue his administration’s construction of a border wall in Texas’s Big Bend region, including parts of Big Bend national park.

In an unsigned, five-page ruling, the nation’s highest court granted the Trump administration’s emergency request to suspend a lower court order that had temporarily stopped the project last month.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court clears way for Trump’s border wall in Texas’s Big Bend

author: Andrew Roth in Washington
description:
President, after talks with Qatari PM, suggests end to war coming ‘fairly soon’ and military escalation not needed

Donald Trump has said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections.

During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says US war in Iran ‘effectively over’ as he plays down escalation concerns

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Tasmanian premier leads tributes for Russell, who earlier this month returned home to ‘see out his days’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor Todd Russell has died aged 54 after recently announcing deteriorating health.

The Tasmanian premier, Jeremy Rockliff, led the tributes on Tuesday morning, saying his thoughts were with Russell’s loved ones.

Continue reading...
title: Todd Russell, Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor, dies aged 54 due to illness

author: Aisha Down and Dan Milmo
description:
Jensen Huang’s close relationship with president means Nvidia CEO’s affair with woman alleged to be working for Beijing is a big deal

A hand on the back, a kiss on the cheek; the footage of Alice Huang’s interaction with Jensen Huang in a Taipei venue last year does not seem particularly remarkable at first glance.

But the Nvidia chief executive’s revelation on Sunday that he had an affair with Ms Huang has given it new significance.

Continue reading...
title: The AI poster boy, the ‘Chinese spy’ and Trump: how an affair may have harmed US security

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Former builder got his big break after restoring the home of a producer who was working on a precursor to the show

Tommy Walsh, the building and DIY expert who appeared on television shows including Ground Force, has died aged 69 after a long illness.

Walsh started his career as a professional builder before rising to fame alongside Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock on the popular BBC garden makeover show from 1997 to 2005.

Continue reading...
title: Tommy Walsh, co-presenter of BBC’s Ground Force, dies aged 69

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Caucus had 100 members in the last Congress, and six of the nine candidates it endorsed won, flipping seats

House progressives, long dismissed as the Democratic party’s leftwing outliers, are heading into the next Congress in larger numbers than ever and vowing to push the new Democratic majority to the left.

The Congressional Progressive caucus said on Sunday it will welcome more than 25 new members, including a record number who won in red districts, expanding its ranks to more than 105 lawmakers.

Continue reading...
title: Progressives head to US House in record numbers after winning red districts

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
‘Not particularly complex’ defrosting hack has been attributed to Iran, with presumption it is linked to others across Europe

Iranian hackers like to send a message.

In 2023 a state-backed group interrupted TV streaming services in the United Arab Emirates to broadcast a deepfake report on the war in Gaza. In the same year, hackers affiliated with Iran displayed the slogan “down with Israel” on the screens of water-control equipment made by an Israeli firm.

Continue reading...
title: Cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers has geopolitical context

author: George Chidi
description:
US representative accuses defense secretary of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers

  • US politics live – latest updates

A Republican lawmaker has moved to force a vote to impeach Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, setting the stage for a showdown over one of the most divisive figures inside Donald Trump’s administration.

Thomas Massie, of Kentucky, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, accusing him of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers.

Continue reading...
title: Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Pete Hegseth

author: Emine Sinmaz and Kevin Rawlinson
description:
TV producer, who was in relationship with ex-comedian that reportedly ended in 2014, accuses him of ‘violence, coercive control and abuse’

  • Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault

Jemima Goldsmith has said Russell Brand physically assaulted her and she accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse”.

The 52-year-old TV producer said she has always been “strongly and unequivocally” on the side of Brand’s victims as she opened up about her own “painful” experience with her former partner in a social media post on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Jemima Goldsmith says ex-partner Russell Brand physically assaulted her

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Calley Means claims officials abandoned Maha agenda and took money from sugar industry leading up to midterms

A former top Trump administration health adviser accused Susie Wiles, whom Donald Trump removed as the White House chief of staff last week, of stalling the so-called “Make America healthy again” (Maha) agenda by prioritizing special interest groups and fundraising before the midterm elections.

Calley Means, who resigned two weeks ago from his job advising Robert F Kennedy Jr, blamed Wiles and other Trump staffers for dropping the ball on the Maha agenda to take money from the sugar industry to fuel the midterms – which Republicans ultimately lost.

Continue
title: Former RFK Jr adviser accuses Trump officials of prioritizing special interest groups over voters

author: Robyn Vinter North of England correspondent
description:
Women say move will be ‘massively detrimental’ to services for vulnerable children, and hit their own pensions

The 33 women waving banners outside a nursery in the South Yorkshire village of Grimethorpe have never been on strike before.

Passing cars beep their horns in support of the workers, who have taken action at six nurseries run by Barnsley council after its Reform UK leadership agreed to transfer them to private companies. They say the move will have a hugely negative impact on the services they provide to vulnerable children, and to their own pensions.

Continue reading...
title: Barnsley workers strike over nursery privatisation by Reform council

author: Emiliano Mellino and Rajeev Syal
description:
Exclusive: Almost two-thirds of visits lead to no arrests and nearly three-quarters are conducted without a warrant

Shabana Mahmood’s ICE-style raid agency has been accused of engaging in “fishing expeditions” after figures disclosed that almost two-thirds of enforcement visits result in no arrests and nearly three-quarters are conducted without a warrant.

The home secretary has hailed the expanded use of immigration enforcement teams, and claimed they will help to secure the UK’s borders by removing a key incentive for irregular migration.

There were 23,538 immigration enforcement engagements such as workplace raids, home raids and spot checks in 2025 - or 60 a day. Of these, 15,578, or 66.1%, resulted in no arrests.

Only 25.81% of visits where a premises was accessed used a warrant. Critics say this suggests the Home Office is launching “fishing expeditions” based on weak intelligence.

Nearly nine out of ten (89%) of leads alleging “immigration crime
title: Mahmood’s ICE-style immigration raid agency accused of ‘fishing expeditions’

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Exclusive: WhatsApp messages show firm pressuring Zubir Ahmed MP to help bring sensitive data into its platform

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Palantir lobbied a health minister to consider extending its AI technology into GP records, stretching its reach into the NHS in a way doctors fear could undermine trust with patients.

The US company, co-founded by the Trump-supporting billionaire Peter Thiel, used a direct WhatsApp channel to argue that “the logic of joining up primary and secondary [care] data is unarguable” and said its software was “ideal” for the job. The push came in February this year despite GP data being expressly ruled out of scope of Palantir’s existing £330m contract with NHS England to run its federated data platform (FDP), which it says has helped cut surgery waiting time
title: Revealed: Palantir lobbied minister to stretch AI tools’ reach to NHS GP records

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Glenn Gibbins sentenced to 150-hours of unpaid work by South Tyneside magistrates over 2024 Facebook post

A Reform party councillor who claimed racist comments about Nigerians were no more than a “bit of fun” has been handed a community order for posting grossly offensive material.

Glenn Gibbins, who was voted on to Sunderland council in May, wrote on Facebook in March 2024: “Carnt believe the amount of nigerians in town… should melt them all down and fill in the pot holes!!”

Continue reading...
title: Reform UK councillor in Sunderland handed community order after racist ‘joke’ about Nigerians

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Particles from fireworks and bonfires likely to have contributed to levels well above WHO’s daily guideline

Air pollution soared to “very high” levels across urban parts of England on Monday as still, foggy weather kept emissions trapped after a weekend of fireworks and bonfires.

Government monitoring showed 11 sites, mainly in London and Greater Manchester, reached the highest band on its 10-point index for particulate matter in the 24 hours to 10am. A further 27 sites recorded “high” levels across the capital, the north-west, the Midlands, Yorkshire and the east of England.

Continue reading...
title: Air pollution soars as fog traps emissions in England’s urban areas

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Exclusive: MP Chris Ward believes ditching pledges and forming closer ties with EU would protect it from global threats

One of the architects of Keir Stamer’s Brexit red lines has called for Andy Burnham to abandon them at the next election, saying a new relationship with the EU would protect the UK from global threats.

The call is the latest voice from a prominent figure in Starmer’s administration for a faster transition to a far closer European relationship, after the former chancellor Rachel Reeves said it was right for Burnham to consider rejoining.

Continue reading...
title: Labour’s Brexit red lines ready for ‘dignified retirement’, says their co-author

author: Nick Robins-Early
description:
Elon Musk and other finance moguls defend Jensen Huang after he admitted to the affair in an email to employees

Donald Trump, Elon Musk and prominent finance moguls have expressed their support for embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as the head of the world’s most valuable chip company faces an internal investigation over a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

“I have not ​spoken to him about it,” Trump told reporters on Sunday. “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on. I’m sure, I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job”.

Continue reading...
title: Silicon Valley and Trump rally behind Nvidia CEO after his affair with alleged Chinese spy

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Exclusive: Cross-party call for ethnicity options to be broadened beyond ‘English’ being only within ‘White’ category

Britons should be able to define themselves as both black and English, according to senior MPs who are calling to broaden the range of ethnicity options in the census.

The cross-party push is a riposte to Reform UK politicians who have claimed that people from minority ethnic backgrounds cannot have English ethnic identity.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Black English’ and ‘Asian English’ should be census options, MPs say

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
Officers pelted with bottles, stones and fireworks after people try to get their hands on special introductory offer

Police were called to a doner kebab shop in Dortmund, western Germany on Sunday after hundreds of customers stormed the premises in the hope of securing a portion for a one-off rock bottom introductory price.

The owner of the outlet was forced to call the police after becoming overwhelmed by the crowds that turned up for its opening.

Continue reading...
title: Dortmund police attacked as crowd storms kebab shop for €1 doner

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Disgraced actor and comedian, 51, was described as a ruthless and manipulative sexual predator during trial

  • Russell Brand sentencing – live updates

Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for raping a fan and sexually assaulting three other women at the height of his showbusiness career.

Brand, 51, was found guilty after a four-week trial at Southwark crown court in which he was described as a ruthless and manipulative sexual predator.

Continue reading.
title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault

author: Nino Bucci Justice and courts reporter
description:
Exclusive: Body-worn camera footage shows woman pulled off bench and a Taser activated despite ‘putting up no resistance’, magistrate says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A magistrate has criticised “exceedingly heavy-handed” ACT police officers who Tasered an Aboriginal woman with an intellectual disability during a routine arrest.

The woman, named Emma, pleaded with officers not to use the stun gun on her and told them she was unarmed during the arrest at a Canberra bus stop in January.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Exceedingly heavy-handed’: ACT police criticised by magistrate for Tasering disabled Aboriginal woman

author: Ben Smee Queensland state correspondent
description:
Prosecutors dropped cases because survivors ‘didn’t act how a rape victim should’, Australian Institute of Criminology review of 19,000 sexual assault cases finds

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queensland police put sexual assault investigations “on the backburner” because detectives were overworked and under pressure to prioritise cases linked to political issues such as youth crime, a major new study has found.

The report, published this month by the Australian Institute of Criminology, sought to investigate why so many sexual assault complaints – about two-thirds of those made to
title: ‘Settle down’ and ‘do your own swabs’: how alleged rape victims are treated in Queensland revealed in major report

author: Patrick Commins
description:
EVs and home batteries are in Treasury crosshairs despite a better economic case for scaling back nuclear-powered submarines and diesel fuel rebates for miners

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

As Jim Chalmers, the treasurer, comes under increasing pressure to fight inflation by slashing spending in the mid-year budget update, the drumbeat is loudest for cuts in one specific area: green energy subsidies for households.

Receiving the most focus is the cheaper home batteries program, which from July last year has offered a taxpayer-backed 30% rebate to households and businesses.

<
title: There’s more than a whiff of politics to the sudden call to slash Labor’s green energy subsidies

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Call for overhaul of manually operated level crossings after delivery worker was killed by passenger train in Kent

An Amazon delivery driver was killed by a train after he drove his van on to railway tracks at a manually operated level crossing, apparently without realising he needed to open the exit gate first, an official investigation has reported.

Safety inspectors said there was “an obvious risk of further tragedy”, with a second similar fatal event still being investigated, and called for an overhaul of this type of crossing.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Obvious risk of further tragedy’ at rail crossing type at which Amazon driver died, inquiry finds

author: Martin Belam
description:
Jensen Huang reportedly had close relationship ‌with Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to ‌Beijing. Plus, tennis legend Billie Jean King tells all

• Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been placed under “independent investigation” by the tech company after reports emerged he had been “the target of a foreign intelligence effort”, namely a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who is accused of passing information to ‌Beijing. Nvidia stock is down 5% in pre-market trading as a result.

The company’s board said in a statement that while it had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its i
title: Nvidia stocks tumble as CEO investigated over spy claims | First Thing

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
President’s admission appears at odds with the elevation of immigration hardliner

  • Trump admits deportation policy was ‘too tough’ despite Miller promotion

  • Sign up for US Breaking News email

Stephen Miller, the influential architect of Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, is due to start as White House chief of staff</
title: Deportation policy ‘might have been too tough’, says Trump, as Miller starts chief-of-staff role – US politics live

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Troubled utility lobbies for deadline on part of the debt to be extended to March 2028

Thames Water has asked its creditors for more time to pay back billions of pounds in debt, as the water company scrambles to keep itself afloat.

The UK’s largest water company said it had proposed an “interim” deal under which the deadline to pay off an unspecified portion of the £20bn of debt on its balance sheet would be extended from 2027 to March 2028.

Continue reading...
title: Thames Water asks creditors for more time to help repay £20bn debt pile

author: Kevin Rawlinson and agency
description:
Drivers warned to take care as ‘perfect’ weather conditions for mist affect areas of England, Wales and Northern Ireland

Thick fog will shroud much of the southern half of England, the eastern half of Wales and most of Northern Ireland throughout the early part of the week, forecasters have said, as commuters are told to expect delays.

There was disruption to flights at Heathrow airport on Monday, while an incident involving 30 vehicles closed a major road in Kent on Saturday evening.

Continue reading...
title: Fog shrouding swathes of UK likely to disrupt transport early this week

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Louise Haigh is expected to agree to cut a target for EV sales by about a quarter

The Tories have criticised the Scottish government for posting a message on its X social media account about a Sikh festival at 11am yesterday – as the nation was observing the two-minute silence for Remembrance Sunday. Harriet Cross, the shadow Scottish secretary, said:

It is hard to see their decision to post about a Sikh festival at precisely 11am, at the very moment that people across the country were observing a two-minute silence to honour our war dead, as a coincidence.

There is no reason why they couldn’t have recognised both - not least out of respect to the 83,000 Sikhs killed fighting in both World Wars.

Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, said he plans to introduce new legislation to introduce mandatory human rights due diligence for companies, which will require
title: Polanski says Labour has ‘shocking record’ on climate issues as ministers expected to cut EV targets for car industry – UK politics live

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Terrorism investigation was opened after attacker opened fire in a market square

The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said some progress had been made on what the “security infrastructure” of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia.

Rubio’s comments on Sunday come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with the talks expected to focus on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and steps to end the war.

Continue reading...
title: Poland’s justice minister says investigation into Kraków shooting will aim to establish if the 24-year-old acted alone – Europe live

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Residents of Astley in Greater Manchester will tell public inquiry next week of ‘cacophony’ of noise causing sleep deprivation and depression

When Stephen Retford retired from the police in 2006, he looked forward to a quiet life after nearly three decades catching villains. But now the former detective has landed another big case – one that is extremely close to home.

“It’s the total injustice of it,” the 70-year-old seethed, staring up at the 18-metre-high mega-warehouse that looms over the quiet village of Astley in Greater Manchester. Residents are up in arms about the “monster” construction, likening it to having a “cruise ship in our back garden”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s a feeling of being screwed over’: once-quiet village despairs over ‘monster’ warehouse

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
‘It’s pretty obvious that there are all sorts of people making all sorts of comments,’ Murray Watt says after budget savings meeting

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The environment minister, Murray Watt, has urged ministers to stop undermining the treasurer, Jim Chalmers, as Labor struggles to sell its budget and looks to cut popular clean energy subsidies to help with the fight against inflation.

Cabinet ministers met again on Monday to discuss potential budget savings to be included in next month’s mid-year update, part of efforts to reducing spending to ease pressure on the economy.
title: Stop undermining Jim Chalmers, environment minister urges Labor colleagues

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Ben Carroll refuses to be drawn on latest opinion poll that puts Labor at all-time low of just 18%, behind One Nation on 21% and the Coalition on 33%

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian Labor MPs are both sceptical and seriously concerned about a new poll ahead of the state election showing the party trailing third behind One Nation, with its primary vote at an all-time low of just 18%.

The DemosAU/PremierNational, first published by the Herald Sun on Monday, showed Labor’s primary vote share has crashed s
title: Victorian election 2026: Concern and scepticism among Labor MPs as new poll shows party trailing One Nation

author: Nino Bucci and Jack Larkin
description:
Inquiry into allegations of corruption begins block of hearings focused on 2022 level crossing removal project

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The royal commission into allegations of corruption on Victorian Big Build projects has heard a major construction company feared putting the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU) offside because of its close links to the Daniel Andrews Labor government.

The first block of hearings under the commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria will
title: CFMEU ‘enjoy a significant level of influence’ over Victorian government, Big Build royal commission hears

author: Anne Davies
description:
Chris Minns and human rights commissioner lambast comments made by Stuart Bonds, who leads party’s NSW upper house ticket

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales premier and the Australian Human Rights Commission have criticised comments by the man who heads One Nation’s upper house ticket in NSW after he said Australians faced demographic replacement unless “mass migration” was curtailed.

Chris Minns described Stuart Bonds’ comments as “frankly outrageous and racist”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Outrageous and racist’: premier responds to NSW One Nation candidate’s claim Australians are being ‘demographically replaced’

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Danielle Madgwick died in regional NSW in September after suffering multiple stab wounds to her upper body

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Family members of a man accused of the domestic violence murder of a 23-year-old woman in south-western New South Wales have been charged with being accessories to the alleged crime.

Emergency services were called to a Wagga Wagga home on the morning of 19 September where they found Danielle Madgwick suffering multiple stab wounds to her upper body. She died at the scene.

Continue reading...
title: Wagga Wagga family members of alleged DV murderer charged with being accessories after the fact

author: Robert Mackey
description:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters

Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).

Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary
